candidates.rationale: Floors margin at zero so loss-making quarters don't distort the ranking, then scales by asset efficiency: firms that are simultaneously profitable and efficient at using assets reconstruct a robust DuPont-style profitability signal distinct from the reported ROA field.

Earnings-quality risk is a threshold effect: only the most aggressive positive-accrual firms (income running ahead of cash flow) get downgraded, while every conservative-accrual firm ties at the top, sharpening the accrual anomaly with an asymmetric read.

Among firms not currently posting losses, price rising in lockstep with volume over the last two weeks signals informed accumulation confirming the quality thesis, favoring profitable names getting fresh conviction buying over those drifting on thin interest.

Severity of unprofitability (zero for profitable firms) interacted with how close price sits to its own 90-day high flags distressed names trading rich relative to their own range as overextended, while genuinely profitable names near their highs get confirmed.

Measures whether the market's price path over the trailing quarter has actually tracked the firm's profitability trajectory; low co-movement flags a lagging repricing opportunity where fundamentals moved but price hasn't caught up.

Normalizes operating efficiency by financial leverage to isolate efficiency achieved organically rather than through balance-sheet risk-taking, a cleaner risk-adjusted quality measure than either raw ratio alone.

Rewards firms that stayed profitable across roughly the trailing three quarters rather than a single snapshot, capturing earnings persistence/reliability that a point-in-time ROA level can't distinguish from a one-off spike.

Gates the overnight gap direction by profitability: a positive overnight gap in a name that is actually earning money reads as fresh confirming information being priced in, while the same gap in a loss-maker carries no such quality backing.

Requires firms to rank highly on both accumulated per-share capital base and current capital efficiency simultaneously, an AND-gate compounder signal that a single ratio or either field alone can't express.

Chooses which profitability lens fits the balance-sheet regime: for highly levered firms, asset-level profitability already nets out how much debt-funded balance sheet was needed to generate earnings, a fairer quality read than operating margin alone; for low-leverage firms operating margin is used directly since balance-sheet distortion is minimal.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.

Working memory: rules written after earlier rounds on this island, oldest first. Apply them.
  1. Short-window raw price differences are return-equivalent for cheap_screen, not just price ratios: TS_DELTA($close, 3) failed twice under different partners this round (|t| 0.47, 0.55). Avoid <=5-day TS_DELTA on a bare OHLC field as a standalone leg.
  2. DELAY's lag argument decorrelates like a TS_MEAN window: wrapping a previously-bare leaf in DELAY(field, 1), or re-lagging an existing DELAY, failed the correlation gate twice this round (rho 0.976, 0.819). Edit a structural node instead of a DELAY lag alone.
  3. TS_MIN($low, w) at a small window is a near-substitute for bare $low inside an extremum ratio — swapping one for the other, or just re-windowing the TS_MIN, didn't decorrelate (rho 0.954, 0.871). Vary the ratio's structure, not which extremum window feeds it.
  4. TS_CORR(ABS($return), TS_RANK($volume, w), 63) accepted at 3.420, so the ABS(return)/TS_RANK(volume) fix holds beyond the previously-validated 21-day correlation window — keep varying this window rather than treating the pairing as used up.
  5. RANK(eps) - RANK(X) and RANK(eps)/X are now closed for X = TS_RANK($dollar_volume) at any window (21 vs 63 hit rho 0.936), ($close-$low)/$high (rho 1.000 vs the /$close version), and ABS(TS_DELTA($dollar_volume,63)) as a crossover donor (only 2 shared nodes). Fuse eps with a second operator instead: multiply by a CS_ZSCORE/TS_CORR cross-term, or apply MIN/MAX truncation to eps before combining.
  6. MIN($earnings_per_share, 0) downside truncation is a new, currently-productive eps transform (2 of 7 accepts this round, fitness 1.298 and 1.859). Push it further before it saturates: try MAX(eps, 0) upside truncation, or MIN/MAX truncation on $roe, $roa, $accrual_gap, or $leverage.
  7. A guarded denominator already used in an archive member (TS_MEAN($dollar_volume,63)+eps, TS_STD($close,126)+eps, TS_RANK($volume,63)+eps) blocks any numerator-only swap via archive_subtree - 3 of this round's 7 archive_subtree rejects changed only the numerator or an outer multiplier and still collided.
  8. Check candidate proposals against accepts made earlier in this same round, not only the archive snapshot from round start - one reject this round shared 4 nodes with a CS_ZSCORE(dollar_volume-rank) diff structure accepted moments earlier in the same batch.
  9. Fundamental-vs-fundamental rank differences keep collapsing across different accounting lines even when the fields look distinct: operating_margin vs roa hit rho 0.860, eps*asset_turnover vs accrual_gap hit rho 0.805. When using a plain rank-difference, pair a fundamental against a price/volume leg, not another fundamental.
  10. A single window, field, or lone-denominator swap inside an otherwise-unchanged 4+ node kernel still fails correlation: TS_RANK($dollar_volume,21 vs 63) hit rho 0.936, TS_MEAN($close,21) vs raw $close hit rho 0.998. Change an inner operator or add a structurally different leg, not just one parameter.
  11. Return-volatility differentials (TS_STD($return,5)-TS_STD($return,21)) and volume-threshold COUNT or dollar_volume-rank terms failed cheap_screen as the second leg regardless of which fundamental (leverage, accrual_gap, operating_margin, eps/leverage) they were paired with, or whether combined by product or difference (4 rejects, |t| 0.04-0.43). These need a stronger fundamental-side transform (delta, or multiplying two fundamentals together) before pairing.
  12. 3 of 20 rejects (15%) were exact within-run duplicates of an earlier proposal this round. Track proposed expressions during generation within the round to avoid resubmitting.

For each proposal give a one-line economic rationale: what mechanism would make
this predict returns. "It is a momentum variant" is not a mechanism.
